proof.criterion: A2, A3 (R1, R2): bare keys and #ids store references under their targets by the spec's boundary, existence and scope rules, beyond the shared table's rows

proof.observed: 29 bare-key rows and 11 #id rows stored exactly as Design 1-3 say (possessive, parenthesis, code span, fenced code, table cell, strikethrough, quote,  , comma, '?', markdown link destination: edge; lowercase, leading zero, decimal, /spec, letter suffix, after slash, #suffix, inside an http URL, double suffix, &, email, after a letter, 11-letter key, Unicode hyphen: none); a key whose issue is created later is linked only by rebuild-refs, and a cross-project key once its issue exists is indexed; a human comment edited twice moves its edges and then drops them; an issue comment's #q9 is indexed by the scope drain once q9 is added to the spec and dropped once q9's block is removed; a 3000-key body stores one edge per existing issue in 435 ms; 20 concurrent comments each carry both edges; an ask's text is indexed; refs_owed drains to 0; rebuild-refs adds only the two edges the spec's Decisions predict.
